item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: PM says government 'will not freeze teen deportations', at least two men shot in Malmö, and more news from Sweden on Wednesday.

item.title: 'I'm done with Sweden': Why citizenship changes are making skilled workers leave
item.description: An overwhelming majority of the readers who answered The Local's survey are either considering leaving Sweden or have already decided to as a result of the country's new stricter citizenship laws, with the retroactive application the most off-putting element.

item.title: '4-hour queues': Europe's airlines and airports fear summer travel chaos
item.description: Airlines across Europe have called on EU chiefs to review the ongoing roll-out for the EES biometric border checks amid fears the system will lead to border chaos this summer.

item.title: Swedish PM says no plans for a freeze on teen deportations
item.description: Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said on Tuesday that his government would not bend to pressure over teen deportations and impose a temporary freeze, allowing recent high profile cases to stay in the country.

item.title: How can you show proof of Swedish and civics knowledge for citizenship?
item.description: Citizenship applicants will need to prove knowledge of Swedish language and civics from June 6th – even if they applied before this date. The only problem? Sweden’s citizenship tests won’t be ready then. How else can you prove you meet the requirements?

item.title: Swedes are far more pro-migration than you think
item.description: Swedes are not opposed to immigration, they’re opposed to immigration that doesn’t benefit them. Throwing working people or their families out of the country is bad politics, argues James Savage.

item.title: Swedish PM: 'Not feasible to revoke permanent residencies at present'
item.description: Sweden's prime minister Ulf Kristersson has said a proposal to revoke existing permanent residency permits cannot be enacted in its present form, and needs to be changed so that more of those affected can get citizenship.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: orka
item.description: Orka is a word that you’ll hear a lot, and is a key to understanding young Swedish people’s conversations.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Board member resigns from Migration Agency committee, funeral for 25-year-old murdered on Christmas Eve, and more news from Sweden on Thursday.

item.title: What are the proposed solutions to Sweden's teen deportation problem?
item.description: Teen deportations – the deportation of young adults after they turn 18 – is now Sweden's biggest political news story, with the opposition piling pressure on the government to take action, and the government parties split on how to respond.
